title: Everything You Know About Alexander the Great Is Wrong #history #alexander #myths
description:
Everything you know about Alexander the Great... Alexander wept because there were no worlds left to conquer, or did he?

Son of Zeus, the horse no one could ride, the Gordian knot cut with a sword, an empire from Greece to India and not one battle lost. Or so the story goes. The battles are real: Issus, Gaugamela, the Hydaspes. But Plutarch says he wept because the worlds were endless and he did not rule even one. And no Greek of his time called him "the Great": in the texts that survive, the name first appears in a Roman comedy, Plautus' Mostellaria, about 200 BC. So was he great... or did Rome make him great?

Sources: Plutarch, Life of Alexander 2-6 and On Tranquility of Mind 466D; Arrian, Anabasis 2.3; Plautus, Mostellaria (c. 200 BC).
Pictures: Alexander Mosaic, House of the Faun, Pompeii (photo TyB, CC BY 2.0); André Castaigne, The Taming of Bucephalus (1898); Jean-François Godefroy, Alexander and the Gordian Knot; head of a philosopher, perhaps Plutarch, Archaeological Museum of Delphi (public domain).
